$comment: THE ONE FILE TO EDIT. Every name the website and the backend share lives here,
so nothing is typed twice and nothing drifts.
public.*   is compiled into the browser bundle. Safe to be read by anyone.
aws.*      names the resources SAM creates (backend/template.yaml).
email.*    who the Lambda sends to, and who it sends as.
limits.*   enforced in the browser AND again in the Lambda.
SECRETS NEVER GO IN THIS FILE. There are none to hold any more: the bot
check runs inside the Lambda. This file is committed.
info@finlabsindia.biz is the identity already verified in SES (ap-south-1,
DKIM passing), so SES is the channel from the start and Reply-To works —
hitting reply in the inbox answers the person who wrote in.
Everything routes to that one address on purpose. If the account is still
in the SES sandbox it can only send TO verified addresses, and that is the
only one. Split hr@ out once it is verified, or once production access is
The website still shows @finlabsindia.com addresses to visitors. That is a
separate question from where these notifications land, and is being left
until the real staff domain is confirmed.

retention.$comment: Matches the Privacy Notice. The Lambda writes a TTL on every row and S3 expires CVs on a lifecycle rule, so the promise enforces itself.
